subject: Proposal: Premium SLA + Dataplane Latency Commitment for Sage Cloud renewal
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@sagecloud.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sagecloud.com>, procurement@sagecloud.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal ask: latency SLO + 24/7 oncall for upcoming term

Hi Diego / Marissa,

Quick context: our renewal window for Sage Cloud Platform is mid-November and the execs want a clearer ops commitment before we sign. Two asks from our side:

- Can Redwood commit to a P95 token-generation latency of <= 150ms for our production model endpoints (dataplane in us-west) in the renewed SOW?
- We need Premium support (24/7 oncall + 30-min response for Sev 1) as an uplift on the existing contract. Our expected average QPS will double after the end-of-year feature rollout, and we want a burst reservation and an oncall handoff process documented.

I attached a short procurement timeline (procurement wants final SOW + SLA amendment by 11/10).

What would you need from us to make the latency/ops commitment? Also please confirm any impact on list price or minimum commitment.

Thanks,
Elaine
Elaine Park
Senior Program Manager, Sage Cloud
Attachments: SageCloud_procurement_timeline.pdf
From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@sagecloud.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sagecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal ask: latency SLO + 24/7 oncall for upcoming term

Hi Elaine / Tom — thanks for the clear asks and timeline. Short answer: we can support both items, but will propose two commercial/ops paths so you have tradeoffs on reserve capacity and pricing. Drafts attached.

Option A (Committed SLO + Premium Support):
- P95 latency commitment: <= 150ms for specified endpoints in us-west on the renewed term.
- Support: 24/7 oncall with 30-min P1 response; oncall escalation playbook and monthly incident review.
- Capacity: reserved pool sized for 2x baseline QPS with burst buffer.
- Commercial: 18% uplift over current list, or 10% uplift + one-time credit to align to budget.

Option B (SLO with progressive roll-in):
- Start with performance target (P95 <= 200ms) and commit to 150ms after a 60-day stabilization and tuning window. Lower uplift but no one-time credit.

I'll attach a draft SLA amendment and a mutual action plan with dates; Marissa and I can run through the commercial recommendation and return with a final SOW/DocuSign link by 11/09 if you pick Option A. Can we schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to agree on the option?

--
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLA-Amendment-Draft-2026.docx, Mutual-Action-Plan-SageCloud.xlsx
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal ask: latency SLO + 24/7 oncall — commercial ask

Priyom — forwarding Elaine's ask and Diego's two-option proposal. Quick summary: customer will sign if we can commit to P95<=150ms + 24/7 oncall and a reserved burst pool sized for ~2x. Procurement needs final SOW by 11/10.

Can we approve a 10% one-time credit to meet their budget if we go with Option A? Ops needs to confirm oncall handoff window and whether we can lock the burst reservation behind a 12-month commit.

Diego — I recommend we offer A with the one-time credit; this closes the deal and gives us predictable committed revenue.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-allocations@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal ask: latency SLO + 24/7 oncall — commercial ask

Marissa / Diego — reviewed. Approve the 10% one-time credit (applied to first invoice) for Option A provided ops confirms:
- Reservation for 2x baseline QPS for the 12-month committed term (can be implemented via Dedicated pool tags).
- Formal oncall handoff doc with primary/secondary contacts and escalation path.
- Monthly SLO review cadence; regression alerting tied to the mutual action plan.

Ops (cc'd): can you confirm capacity reservation and oncall handoff SLA by EOD Monday (11/09)? If ops signs off, Diego, proceed with final SOW + DocuSign. I'll pre-approve the pricing exception.

Priyom
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@sagecloud.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@sagecloud.com>, procurement@sagecloud.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Premium SLA + Dataplane Latency Commitment for Sage Cloud renewal

Diego / Marissa — great, thanks for the fast turnaround and the flexibility. Sage Cloud accepts Option A with the 10% one-time credit and the 12-month reserved burst pool. Please:

1) Send the final SOW + SLA amendment with the P95<=150ms metric and the oncall escalation playbook to procurement by end of day.
2) Include the DocuSign link so our procurement team can route for signature.

We plan an operational kickoff the week of 11/15; please include the oncall roster and a first monthly SLO review invite in the packet.

Elaine
Senior Program Manager, Sage Cloud
Attachments referenced: Draft-SOW-Redwood-SageCloud.pdf
